overview: Two ways to profile a microbial community — one reads a single universal marker gene, the other reads everything.
genZNote: One zooms in on a single gene. One opens the whole crowd.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Sequences a targeted, PCR-amplified region of the 16S ribosomal RNA gene, a marker present in all bacteria and archaea, to identify community members.
aspects.valueB: Sequences all DNA present in a sample without targeted amplification, capturing genetic material from every organism present, including function-encoding genes.

aspects.label: Target Scope
aspects.valueA: Targets only the 16S rRNA gene (or a variable region of it) via PCR amplification.
aspects.valueB: Captures the entire genomic content of the sample — all organisms and all genes, not just one marker.

aspects.label: Taxonomic Resolution
aspects.valueA: Usually resolves to genus level reliably; species- or strain-level resolution is often limited.
aspects.valueB: Can achieve species- and strain-level resolution, given sufficient sequencing depth.

aspects.label: Functional Information
aspects.valueA: Provides essentially no direct functional gene information — only taxonomic identity.
aspects.valueB: Directly captures functional genes (e.g. antibiotic resistance genes, metabolic pathways), enabling functional profiling.

aspects.label: Cost and Data Volume
aspects.valueA: Lower cost and smaller, more manageable data volume per sample.
aspects.valueB: Higher cost and much larger data volume, requiring more computational resources.

aspects.label: Bias Considerations
aspects.valueA: Subject to PCR primer bias, which can under- or over-represent certain taxa.
aspects.valueB: Avoids PCR amplification bias but can be skewed by host DNA contamination in low-biomass samples.

aspects.label: Typical Applications
aspects.valueA: Rapid, cost-effective community composition surveys (e.g. gut microbiome diversity studies).
aspects.valueB: In-depth functional and taxonomic characterization, novel organism discovery, antibiotic resistance gene surveillance.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Targets one marker gene, cheaper, genus-level.
aspects.valueB: Sequences all DNA, more expensive, species-level with functional data.
